```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(TidyPanel)
```

The four bundled CSV files are fictional examples with three input rows each.
They contain no personal records or development datasets.

## Numbers

```{r numbers}
numbers <- read_messy_panel(system.file(
  "extdata", "demo_01_numbers.csv", package = "TidyPanel", mustWork = TRUE
))
numbers
```

The record codes keep their leading zeros. The amount column becomes numeric,
including a negative amount and a missing value.

## Dates

```{r dates}
dates <- read_messy_panel(system.file(
  "extdata", "demo_02_dates.csv", package = "TidyPanel", mustWork = TRUE
))
dates
```

The date column becomes a `Date` column. A missing reading stays missing.

## Subtotals And Periods

```{r subtotals}
panel <- read_messy_panel(
  system.file(
    "extdata", "demo_03_subtotals.csv", package = "TidyPanel", mustWork = TRUE
  ),
  auto_pivot = TRUE,
  return_audit = TRUE
)
panel$data
panel$audit
```

The total row is excluded and the two yearly columns become a long table.

## Caller-Declared Missing Tokens

```{r missing-tokens}
missing_tokens <- read_messy_panel(
  system.file(
    "extdata", "demo_04_missing_tokens.csv", package = "TidyPanel", mustWork = TRUE
  ),
  na_strings = "MISSING"
)
missing_tokens
```

The fictional token `MISSING` becomes a missing reading because it is explicitly
declared. The zero reading stays zero, and record codes remain literal text.
Choose missing markers from your own source's definitions, not this example.

Agents can run `Rscript --vanilla exec/tidypanel.R describe` to obtain all four
example request templates, including their installed input paths and options.
Choose a new output directory for each job; example discovery creates no files.

For your own table, supply its file path instead of a bundled example.
